subject: Acme bake-off — discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme bake-off — discovery recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Anita,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid discussion. I wanted to recap the key pain points, what success looks like for the bake-off, and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Pain points we heard
- Inconsistent latency and throughput from current self-hosted vLLM/TGI endpoints at peak traffic.
- High per-token cost and unpredictable scaling behavior during business hours.
- Need for predictable SLAs and auditability (data residency + logs) for customers in EMEA.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Inference: vLLM (self-hosted) + some TGI endpoints for experiments
- Orchestration: Kubernetes with mixed GPU fleet (A100 + T4)
- Eval/bench: internal scripts + a Golden test set for core LLM behaviors

Acme bake-off acceptance criteria (initial)
- Latency: p95 generation time for 512-token prompts <= 200ms (single-request median target < 120ms)
- Throughput: sustained 100 concurrent requests (avg prompt length ~256 tokens) with < 250ms p95
- Cost: comparable or better than current $0.0009/token blended cost (target: <= $0.0006/token at scale)
- Quality: no statistically significant regression on your prompt/response eval set vs current baseline
- Ops: evidence of observability (token-level traces), audit logs, and ability to run in your VPC (data residency)

Benchmarks we propose Redwood to run initially
1) Baseline run vs: (a) your vLLM infra, (b) TGI hosted test instance, (c) Redwood hosted endpoints (and Dedicated if you want)
2) Workloads: 1) synthetic high-throughput (short prompts), 2) production-like mix (your golden set), 3) long-context scenarios (2k tokens)
3) Metrics: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU memory footprint, cost per 1M tokens, and failure/error rates

Attachments: I attached a starter benchmarks spreadsheet (acme-bakeoff-benchmarks.xlsx) with suggested workloads and measurement columns, and a short Redwood prod architecture doc for context (redwood-prod-architecture.pdf).

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm acceptance criteria above and share the Golden eval set (or a subset we can use) + any runbook/constraints (data residency, allowed IP ranges).
- Us (Redwood): finalize test plan (we'll propose exact commands/configs), run initial baseline tests (can run in our hosted env or provide config to run in your cluster), and share results + follow-up demo.
- Schedule: goal to run first baseline by the week of 2026-06-01; open to adjusting based on your timelines.

If that aligns I’ll get Dev and Logan to draft the test commands and a short checklist for access (keys/credentials + IP allowlist).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0143

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off — discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and mostly aligns with our internal view. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Data residency: EMEA customers require logs and audit trails to stay in our EU region. We'll need Redwood to demonstrate VPC/on-prem options for the bake-off.
- Benchmarks: please include GPU memory footprint (we're constrained on node sizes) and cold-start numbers for scaled-up replicas.
- Who runs tests: we prefer Redwood to run an initial baseline against your hosted endpoints so we can validate the approach; after that, we can trial a run in our cluster with help from Dev/Logan.

I can share a stripped-down Golden eval set (PII removed) today and will loop in infra to provide an allowlist for any IPs you need.

Jordan
Head of ML Engineering
Acme Inc.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off — discovery recap & next steps (technical plan)

Marissa / Logan,

Putting together the initial technical plan based on the acceptance criteria. High-level approach:

1) Baseline run (Redwood hosted)
- Models: use the same model family you flagged (llama-2-70b / quantized 4-bit variant) + a Redwood-verified 34B variant for comparison.
- Commands: run synthetic throughput (wrk-style) against our same-config endpoints, record p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec.
- Memory: capture max GPU memory and per-request KV cache footprint.

2) In-cluster validation (optional)
- Provide helm chart and minimal manifests. We'll provide a docker image and a small wrapper script to run your golden set.

3) Tests to capture
- Latency distributions with concurrent clients (10/50/100), cold-start (scale from 0 replicas), and cost estimate based on token count.
- Compare against your vLLM/TGI exports by running the same prompts and measuring response similarity (BLEU/embedding-distance threshold you define).

Logistics we need from Acme
- Golden eval set (or subset) + expected output checks (oracles)
- Allowlist IPs (we'll share endpoints) or a service account for running in your VPC
- Estimated concurrency profile and expected peak QPS

I'll draft exact shell commands and a k8s manifest snippet this afternoon; Marissa, do you want me to attach the scripts to the HubSpot record or share on the Drive?

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off — discovery recap & next steps

Thanks everyone — that plan looks good. A few quick points before we schedule: 

- Confirm Redwood will run the first baseline in your hosted env (yes to that).
- We will provide the Golden eval subset and IP allowlist by EOD today.
- Acceptance criteria: we want p95 <= 200ms (512 tokens) and cost <= $0.0006/token; quality checks will be the golden set embedding-distance threshold (I will include the threshold in the dataset doc).

Let's lock a date for the bake-off week: 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-05 works for us. Can Redwood reserve a time window to run the hosted baselines that week and then support a follow-up run in our cluster?

Jordan
Head of ML Engineering, Acme Inc.
